title: Make the call
tagline: What would you do with mixed clues?
description: Weigh imperfect evidence as a lake manager. A warning, a sample, or more waiting?
projectQuestion: Who needs a warning, and what extra evidence would change your decision?
how: Every round is invented. You choose with incomplete evidence, then see the hidden teaching outcome. You cannot infer toxins from the photo or sensor alone.

Posting a warning costs 2 points for effort and disruption. A false alarm costs another 3. Waiting during a toxic event costs 12. Waiting during a quiet round costs 0. These are teaching points, not dollars or official policy.

Sampling costs 3 points and reveals the hidden result in this game. You then decide whether to warn or wait. Real sampling is delayed, uncertain and not perfect; our instant test is a deliberate simplification.
Lower total cost is better in this invented game. It does not identify a single best real-world policy. Different communities may weigh consequences differently.
prompt: Before you try it: what evidence would you want to collect?

challenges.title: Make a call
challenges.goal: Complete one round and inspect what your choice missed or found.
challenges.hint: Choose a warning, a sample, or waiting.

challenges.title: Buy more evidence
challenges.goal: Send a sampling crew and then make a decision.
challenges.hint: Sampling has a cost, but it can change your next choice.

challenges.title: Keep a decision record
challenges.hint: Compare the evidence before the reveal with the outcome after it.

challenges.title: Compare tradeoffs
challenges.goal: Finish a run, then use Replay to try a different strategy.
challenges.hint: No perfect policy is promised. Track misses as well as false alarms.

omissions: No real public-health advice, agency policy, cost estimate or real-time event.
Instant perfect sampling is unrealistic. Real warnings require local authority and current evidence.
No score measures the value of a life or the team’s real solution.
warning: Simulated game. Invented evidence, outcomes and point costs. Not lake-management advice.

rounds.title: A quiet-looking shore
rounds.sensor: Temperature 29°C; no local toxin test yet.
rounds.photo: A citizen reports a small loose mat near shore.
rounds.lesson: A quiet-looking surface and low model score can miss a local mat hazard.

rounds.title: A green patch
rounds.photo: A citizen sees green floating leaves.
rounds.lesson: Look-alikes and muddy runoff can trigger a false alarm. That does not make photos a safety test.

rounds.title: Several clues agree
rounds.sensor: Warm, slow-moving water; pigment signal elevated.
rounds.photo: More than one person reports loose mats.
rounds.lesson: Several clues can support further action, but only the invented reveal gives certainty here.

rounds.title: A gap in the record
rounds.forecast: The model has no recent input.
rounds.lesson: No report is not proof that no event exists.

rounds.title: A changed scene
rounds.photo: One old photo is being shared again.
rounds.lesson: Evidence needs a time and place. An old photo may describe a different day.

rounds.title: Conflicting signals
rounds.sensor: Pigment signal is low in open water.
rounds.photo: Shoreline photo is too blurred to identify.
rounds.lesson: Uncertainty is part of a decision. A false alarm and a miss have different consequences.
